description: Granular synthesiser with 16 sample slots and 16 incoming-signal voices: grains are spawned from whichever of the 32 voices the weighting picks, each with its own size, pitch, envelope and position

params.text: Sets how often a grain is spawned, one every 10 seconds to 1000 a second
Varies the time until the next grain at random by up to half the spawn period either way, 0 to 100%
Adds an offset to every start point drawn on the START grid, 0 to 100% of the sample
Adds an offset to every stop point drawn on the STOP grid, -100% to 0 of the sample
Adds to every speed drawn on the SPEED grid, -3 to 3, where a negative speed plays that slot backward; at a speed of 0 grains are taken from the start point instead
Adds to every grain length drawn on the GRAIN SIZE grid, which itself spans 1ms to 100ms, so the two together reach 200ms
Adds to every pitch shift drawn on the PITCH grid, -3 to 3, where 1 plays the grain twice as fast and -1 half as fast
Adds to every envelope drawn on the ENVELOPE grid, stepping through none, triangle, Welch, sine, Hanning, Blackman, Nutall, Kaiser, exponential decay and exponential attack
Bends the voice weighting from linear at 0 to logarithmic at 100%, which lowers the chance of the voices drawn quietest
Chooses how the FREEZE and REVERSE inputs are read: as a level that acts while it is above 0V, or as a trigger that switches the voice each time
Draws the random pitch of each grain from a bell curve rather than evenly, so most grains land near the pitch that was drawn
Draws the random panning of each grain from a bell curve rather than evenly, so most grains land near the position that was drawn

inputs.text: The signal recorded into the incoming-signal voices; each polyphonic channel here is a voice of its own, up to 16 of them
Adds an offset to every start point on the START grid, 5V covering the whole sample
Slides the START drawing across the voices, 5V covering the whole height of the grid
Adds to the rotation of the START grid, 5V being 180 degrees
Adds an offset to every stop point on the STOP grid, 5V covering the whole sample
Slides the STOP drawing across the voices, 5V covering the whole height of the grid
Adds to the rotation of the STOP grid, 5V being 180 degrees
Adds an offset to every speed on the SPEED grid, 5V covering the whole -3 to 3 range
Slides the SPEED drawing across the voices, 5V covering the whole height of the grid
Adds to the rotation of the SPEED grid, 5V being 180 degrees
Adds an offset to every value drawn on the VOICE WEIGHTING grid, 5V covering the whole range
Slides the VOICE WEIGHTING drawing across the voices, 5V covering the whole height of the grid
Adds to the rotation of the VOICE WEIGHTING grid, 5V being 180 degrees
Adds to every grain length on the GRAIN SIZE grid, 5V covering the whole range
Slides the GRAIN SIZE drawing across the voices, 5V covering the whole height of the grid
Adds to the rotation of the GRAIN SIZE grid, 5V being 180 degrees
Adds to every pitch shift on the PITCH grid, 5V covering the whole -3 to 3 range
Slides the PITCH drawing across the voices, 5V covering the whole height of the grid
Adds to the rotation of the PITCH grid, 5V being 180 degrees
Adds to how far pitch is allowed to vary at random, 5V covering the whole range; that spread is drawn on the PITCH grid by holding shift
Slides the random pitch spread across the voices, 5V covering the whole height of the PITCH grid
Scales the random pitch spread by the cosine of the angle this sets, 5V being 180 degrees
Adds to every envelope on the ENVELOPE grid, 5V stepping across all ten
Slides the ENVELOPE drawing across the voices, 5V covering the whole height of the grid
Adds to the rotation of the ENVELOPE grid, 5V being 180 degrees
Adds an offset to every value drawn on the PANNING grid, 5V covering the whole range
Slides the PANNING drawing across the voices, 5V covering the whole height of the grid
Adds to the rotation of the PANNING grid, 5V being 180 degrees
Adds to how far panning is allowed to vary at random, 5V covering the whole range; that spread is drawn on the PANNING grid by holding shift
Slides the random panning spread across the voices, 5V covering the whole height of the PANNING grid
Scales the random panning spread by the cosine of the angle this sets, 5V being 180 degrees
Adds to the grain density, 10V covering the whole range
Adds to the density randomness, 10V covering 0 to 100%
A clock here spawns a grain on each rising edge in place of the internal density timer
Stops the matching incoming-signal voice recording, so its grains keep coming from the buffer it already holds; polyphonic, one channel per such voice
Reverses the grains taken from the matching incoming-signal voice; polyphonic, one channel per such voice
Reverses the grains taken from the matching sample slot; polyphonic, one channel per slot
Transposes the grains from the matching sample slot, one volt doubling their rate and one volt below halving it; beyond a volt the scaling is linear rather than per octave
Transposes the grains from the matching incoming-signal voice, one volt doubling their rate and one volt below halving it; beyond a volt the scaling is linear rather than per octave

outputs.text: The left channel of the grains added together
The right channel of the grains added together

notes: a grain is only ever taken from a slot that holds a sample or from a patched input jack, so read a file in with Load Sample 1 or Load Directory before expecting sound
a grid is drawn on by dragging across it, and holding shift while dragging keeps the drag on the band it started on, so one band can be set without disturbing its neighbours
each grid is one display rather than one control per band, so no band can be clicked for a line of its own
right-clicking a grid opens that grid's own menu rather than the module's, and All Maximum, All Minimum, All Half, Triangle, Sine, Ramp and Random fill the grid with that shape
a grid's own right-click menu also carries Flip Horizontal, Flip Vertical, Reduce By Half, Shift Left and Shift Right, which rework what is already drawn on it
on the Grain Pitch and Panning grids a shift-drag sets a range rather than one value, and those two grids carry Reset Range in their own right-click menus as well
menu: Load Sample 1 — reads a WAV file into the first of the sixteen sample slots, and Load Sample 2 through Load Sample 16 fill the rest
Load Directory — reads the WAV files of a folder into the sixteen sample slots
Clear Samples — empties all sixteen sample slots
